cards.text: Friend, the Teacher is talking: the son of David, king in Jerusalem (Eccl 1:1). He's been taking a hard look at life, and now he says that in his futile life he's seen two things. Two things that'll make you stop and go, WAIT, WHAT?

cards.question: In his futile life, what has the Teacher seen happen to a righteous man?

answers.text: He lives long in his righteousness
He is honored by every king

cards.question: True or false: the Teacher has also seen a wicked man die young in his wickedness.

cards.text: Then the Teacher says, "Do not be overly righteous, and do not make yourself too wise." Friend, my eyebrows just climbed up under my chef's hat.

cards.question: The Teacher asks a question about going too far with being righteous and wise. What does he warn could happen?

cards.text: Then he swings the other way, and HARD. Don't be excessively wicked, and don't be a fool.

cards.question: The Teacher warns that if you're excessively wicked or a fool, you could die before your ___.

cards.text: So what's the move? The Teacher says, "It is good to grasp the one and not let the other slip from your hand." Hold on to both? Friend, my mustache is already holding three cookie boxes.

cards.question: The Teacher says the one who ___ God will follow both warnings.

cards.text: Wisdom makes the wise man stronger than ten rulers in a city. TEN rulers, and I can't even get one oven timer to listen to me.

cards.question: Next, the Teacher says something about every person on earth. True or false: he says there is no righteous man on earth who does good and never sins.

cards.text: Then the Teacher says not to pay attention to every word that's spoken. Friend, if I hung on every single beep from my oven timer, I'd never get one cookie box packed.

cards.question: If you hang on every word people say, who does the Teacher say you might hear cursing you?
What reason does the Teacher give for not paying attention to every word that is spoken?

answers.text: You have cursed others many times yourself
Servants are never pleased with anyone
Curses can never harm a wise man

cards.text: All this, the Teacher says, he tested by wisdom, saying, "I resolve to be wise." Friend, that's a big goal. Taller than my chef's hat.

cards.question: When the Teacher sets out to be wise, how does it turn out?

answers.text: He found every answer he sought
He was praised throughout the city

cards.text: Then he looks at everything that exists, and he asks, "Who can fathom it?"

cards.question: True or false: the Teacher says what exists is out of reach and very deep.

cards.text: Out of reach, like me going for the last chocolate chip at the bottom of the big bin with my mustache stretched ALL the way out. Then the Teacher says he directed his mind to understand, to explore, and to search out wisdom and explanations.

cards.question: Besides wisdom and explanations, what else does the Teacher set his mind to understand?

answers.text: The stupidity of wickedness and the folly of madness
The paths of the stars and the depths of the sea
The riches of kings and the strength of armies

cards.text: And here's what he finds more bitter than death: "the woman who is a snare, whose heart is a net, and whose hands are chains."

cards.question: The Teacher says one kind of man escapes the woman who is a snare. Who is it?
True or false: the Teacher says the sinner escapes the woman who is a snare too.

cards.text: Then the Teacher says, "I have discovered this by adding one thing to another to find an explanation." One plus one plus one, friend, that's how I count cookie boxes, and I lose track at FOUR.

cards.question: As he keeps adding things up, the Teacher says his soul was still ___ but not finding.

cards.text: And while he's still searching, he says that among a thousand he has found one upright man, but among all these he has not found one such woman.
Then he lands on the only thing he says he has found, and it's about all mankind. God made mankind upright.

cards.question: God made mankind upright, but the Teacher says something went off track. What did mankind do?

answers.text: They were led astray by kings
They grew tired of doing good

findings.problem: The oven timer joke doesn't share the verse's core action. Verse 7:21 is about hanging on every word and hearing something hurtful about yourself, like your servant cursing you. The joke is about getting distracted by beeps. It also doesn't make sense, because a baker should listen to an oven timer. On top of that, it reuses the oven timer gag from card 10 two cards earlier.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The right answer stands out. 'fears' God is a familiar Bible phrase. 'blames' and 'questions' God sound modern and are easy to rule out, so the baker can pick the answer by tone instead of by meaning.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: This story card is a bare retelling with none of Papa Dorin's voice. Several later cards in stop 2 (cards 7, 12 and 13) are also plain. Cards 7 and 12 sit on sensitive verses, so it's fine for them to stay plain. Cards 3 and 13 have room for a reaction or a laugh and could use some voice.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: This is the passage's closing turn, 'God made mankind upright', and it is told flatly with no reaction from Papa Dorin. That makes it read like a summary instead of his storytelling.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
